units.title: Let's say hello!
units.goal: Saluda, preséntate y deletrea tu nombre.
units.explain: Usa I’m o My name is para presentarte. Good evening es un saludo; good night se usa al despedirse o ir a dormir. Para pedir que deletreen: How do you spell that?
dialog: How do you spell your name?
write: Write a short introduction.
Spell your first name.

units.title: Important dates
units.goal: Habla de días, meses, números y fechas.
units.explain: Días y meses llevan mayúscula. En inglés estadounidense: February 16th; en inglés británico: 16 February. Los números 21–99 que no son decenas llevan guion: twenty-five. Para 1998: nineteen ninety-eight; para 2002: two thousand two (también two thousand and two).
dialog: My birthday is on February sixteenth.
write: When is your birthday?
What day is it today?
When is Christmas?
What is your favorite holiday?
What is your phone number? Use a fictional number if you prefer.

units.title: Occupations
units.explain: What do you do? pregunta por tu ocupación. Usa a antes de sonido consonántico y an antes de sonido vocálico: a teacher, an architect, an engineer. Police officer es una alternativa inclusiva a policeman.
dialog: No, I'm not. I'm an architect.
write: What do you do?
What does a person in your family do?

units.title: Where are you from?
units.explain: Where are you from? → I’m from Colombia. What’s your nationality? → I’m Colombian. Los países y las nacionalidades llevan mayúscula. England y United Kingdom no son equivalentes.
dialog: I'm from the United States. I'm American. Where are you from?
write: What is your name? Where are you from?
Write your country and nationality.

units.title: How's the weather?
units.goal: Describe el clima y la temperatura.
units.explain: How’s the weather? y What’s the weather like? preguntan por el clima. Usa It’s + adjetivo: It’s cold and rainy. Yesterday se refiere al pasado: It was warm yesterday. Las estaciones dependen del hemisferio.
dialog: What was the weather like yesterday?
write: What is the weather like today?
What was the weather like yesterday?

units.title: Let's go shopping!
units.explain: Para describir ropa que alguien lleva puesta: I’m wearing…, He’s wearing…, She’s wearing… El color va antes de la prenda: a pink dress, black pants. Gray y grey son variantes correctas.
dialog: I'm wearing a white T-shirt and blue jeans.
write: What are you wearing today?
Describe an outfit for a cold day.

units.title: My family
units.goal: Habla de tu familia y sus relaciones.
units.explain: Usa ’s para indicar relaciones: Anna is Leo’s mother. How many brothers or sisters do you have? pregunta cuántos hermanos tienes. Puedes describir una familia ficticia si lo prefieres.
dialog: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
write: What is your mother’s name?
How many brothers or sisters do you have?
Do you have any sons or daughters?

units.title: My body
units.goal: Nombra partes del cuerpo y molestias comunes.
units.explain: Usa I have a headache o I have a sore throat para expresar una molestia. Plurales irregulares: foot → feet, tooth → teeth. Hands and fingers se refiere a manos y dedos; feet and toes, a pies y dedos de los pies.
dialog: Do you have a sore throat?
write: Name six parts of the body.
Write two sentences using “I have…” and health vocabulary.

units.title: My daily routine
units.goal: Describe rutinas y di la hora.
units.explain: Usa presente simple para hábitos: I wake up at seven. Past indica minutos después de la hora; to, minutos para la siguiente. 13:30 puede decirse one thirty p.m. o half past one. A las 12:00 puede ser noon (mediodía) o midnight (medianoche), según el contexto.
dialog: What time do you wake up?
I wake up at seven o'clock.
What time do you have lunch?
I have lunch at one p.m.
write: Write your routine with seven times and activities.
What time do you go to bed?

units.title: Places in the city
units.explain: Where’s the library? pregunta por un lugar. How do I get to the museum? pide indicaciones. Usa next to, opposite y between para ubicarlo. Go straight, then turn right at the corner.
dialog: How do I get to the museum?
Turn right at the corner. It's next to the police station.
write: Write directions from a bank to a museum.
Describe two places in your neighborhood.

units.title: In my house
units.explain: There is se usa en singular; there are, en plural. There is a sofa in the living room. There are two bedrooms. Pregunta: How many bedrooms are there in your house? Sink puede estar en el baño o en la cocina.
dialog: How many bedrooms are there in your house?
My favorite room is the living room.
write: How many bedrooms and bathrooms are there in your house?
What is your favorite room?
Classify: bed, stove, toilet, microwave, bedside table, bathtub, rice cooker, wardrobe and sink.

units.title: All about me

groups.title: Personal information
words: What do you like to do in your free time?
¿Qué te gusta hacer en tu tiempo libre?

groups.title: Words to describe
words: Feo/a: juicio que puede resultar ofensivo

units.explain: Usa be para edad y características: I am twenty years old. She is tall. Usa have para rasgos: He has curly hair. Prioriza descripciones neutrales; fat y ugly aparecen en el original, pero pueden resultar hirientes. Puedes usar información ficticia para practicar.
dialog: What do you like to do in your free time?
I like to read and listen to music.
I'm tall. I have brown eyes and curly hair.
write: Introduce yourself: name, age, country, occupation and birthday.
Describe your appearance, your family and your favorite activities.
